content_text_body:
Allowing your team to be autonomous promotes creativity. The goal is to learn how to identify and reverse your tendency to micromanage, and let your team work confidently on their own.

[Getting Serious About Autonomy](video "LiL3_Serious_About_Autonomy")

**Watch**: *Getting Serious About Autonomy*

---

### Do some light reading

Read [10 Warning signs of a Micromanager](http://www.forbes.com/sites/lisaquast/2015/09/07/part-1-10-warning-signs-of-a-micromanager/#4200fbb5252d) to see if this is an issue and how you can identify areas to work on. Then read [How To Overcome Micromanager Tendencies, Part 2](http://www.forbes.com/sites/lisaquast/2015/09/14/how-to-overcome-micromanager-tendencies-part-2/#5cd82e226030) to learn ways to cut back on micromanaging.

### Practice these techniques

Here's a great way to create a new habit of supporting autonomy. Write this down and say it aloud when necessary:

> WHEN I feel the urge to do or redo someone's work, THEN I will clearly communicate what needs to be changed and why it's important.

Make an appointment for yourself in two weeks to reflect on your progress, and ask yourself:

* What did you learn from enabling your team to work independently?

* Was it easier or harder than you'd expected?

* What would you do differently next time?

* Did you notice anything different about you or your team as a result?

* What other things could you do to continue empowering the team?
